text:
maria_ml: Heads-up — saw a consistent 4-6% AWQ accuracy drop on the conversational eval suite when prefetch + continuous batching (pack_by_prefix) are enabled for the fp8 variant. Small repro attached in thread below. Anyone seen something similar?

ajay: Reproduced locally on the micro-harness. Correlates with prefetch_window >= 3 AND pack_by_prefix=true. If we disable packing the regression disappears.

sarah.eng: Can you paste the exact config + model?

maria_ml: Sure — model: redwood/llm-70b-xt-awq-fp8, quant: awq-8-perlayer, runtime flags: 
```
prefetch_enabled = true
prefetch_window = 4
pack_by_prefix = true
continuous_batching = true
kv_cache_versioning = v1
```
Repro steps: send 1k chatty prompts (avg 120 tokens) with mixed prefixes, compare against fp16 baseline. Failure mode: subtle hallucinations and single-token mismatches in ~40/1000 prompts.

nate: From infra side I saw interleaved log lines like: 
```
2026-03-18 12:34:02.123 kvcache WARN mismatch prefix_id: expected=0x7f3 got=0x7f2 src=batch_packer
2026-03-18 12:34:02.124 runtime ERROR kv_fetch validation failed: seq_nonce=42 != stored_nonce=41
```
that smells like a race where prefetch writes a KV for sequence N but packer pulls a different request ordering into the batch that expects N-1.

opsbot: CI run perf-run-2145678950 completed — client-side error rate 4.1% (baseline: 0.6%). See https://ci.redwood.internal/runs/2145678950

ajay: Hypothesis: AWQ's per-layer scaling/zero-points introduce tiny numerical diffs relative to fp16; if a stale or mis-tagged KV is reused the rounding delta is amplified and surfaces as a wrong token. For fp16 the rounding is smaller so same race doesn't break.

maria_ml: Quick spike test: added a lightweight `batch_nonce` into the KV key (kv_prefix_tagging) and a validation check on fetch — if tag mismatch, treat as cache miss. Shadow-run for 5k requests: error rate dropped to 0.9%, but tail latency +~3ms.

sarah.eng: That tradeoff seems reasonable as a canary mitigation. We should gate it to AWQ/fp8 only. Also try reducing prefetch_window to 2 and see if we can avoid tagging perf cost.

nate: Perf numbers for tagged-prefetch (dedicated pool YA) — throughput down 6%, p95 +3ms. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/2145679000. If we only enable on canary 10% it should be fine.

maria_ml: Next steps I propose: 1) run 12h soak with kv-tagging enabled for awq-fp8 on canary hosts, 2) run a control with prefetch_window=2 + pack_by_prefix=false to compare, 3) add metric `kv_prefetch_conflict_count` and alert threshold at 100/hr, 4) open PR for the tagging change and unit tests.

ajay: +1. Please make tagging opt-in via runtime flag `kv_prefetch_tagging=auto|off|on` where `auto` enables only for known quantized runtimes (awq/fp8).

ci-bot: PR opened: gh/redwood/runtime#4857 — "awq: kv-prefetch-tagging to avoid cross-batch kv reuse". Tests: unit + integration.

maria_ml: I'll draft a short runbook for the canary: rollback steps (disable tagging or fallback to fp16 variant), dashboards to watch (kv_prefetch_conflict_count, chatty_eval_error_rate, p95_latency), and post-mortem template.

sarah.eng: Assign rollout plan to @maria_ml and let me know when the 12h soak hits 0.8% or lower. Also add a note to the dedicated capacity team — we may want to coordinate if throughput drops.

maria_ml: Will do. Also logging note: surface the mismatched prefix_id and seq_nonce in a sampled debug log (1/1000) instead of full trace to keep noise down.

ajay: One more experiment idea: try `prefetch_slot_shrink` — allocate prefetch slots to callers by prefix-hash to reduce cross-prefix collisions. Could be a lower-latency mitigation than full tagging.

maria_ml: Good idea, I'll add that as an A/B in the soak.

opsbot: Reminder: post canary we should add an e2e regression test to the onboarding harness for AWQ-fp8 + prefetch + packer combos.

maria_ml: Agreed — opening the follow-ups now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
